props.title: The Great Ziegfeld
props.initialSlug: Extravagant biopic of Broadway's greatest showman

sections.content: **The Great Ziegfeld** (1936) revolutionized the Hollywood musical biopic, setting the template for lavish showbusiness stories that influenced everything from **Funny Girl** (1968) to **Bohemian Rhapsody** (2018). William Powell's portrayal of theatrical impresario Florenz Ziegfeld Jr. captures the essence of Broadway's golden age, while the film's groundbreaking production numbers, particularly "A Pretty Girl Is Like a Melody," showcase MGM's unparalleled production values with its famous rotating wedding cake set piece that required a 70-foot tower and cost $220,000 to film – an astronomical sum for 1936.

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond its immediate era, establishing conventions still seen in modern musical biopics. The rags-to-riches-to-rags narrative structure later appeared in **Coal Miner's Daughter** (1980) and **Walk the Line** (2005). Director Robert Z. Leonard's innovative approach to filming musical numbers, particularly his use of tracking shots and dramatic crane movements, influenced later directors like Vincente Minnelli in **An American in Paris** (1951) and Bob Fosse in **All That Jazz** (1979).

Luise Rainer's portrayal of Anna Held made history as she became the first performer to win consecutive Academy Awards, winning again for **The Good Earth** (1937). Her famous telephone scene became a masterclass in screen acting, demonstrating how to convey complex emotions in a single take. This performance influenced later musical biopic actresses, from Diana Ross in **Lady Sings the Blues** (1972) to Renée Zellweger in **Judy** (2019). SUBHEAD: The Legacy of Ziegfeld's Spectacle

sections.content: The film's recreation of the Ziegfeld Follies' elaborate stage shows influenced decades of Hollywood musicals, from **Easter Parade** (1948) to **Moulin Rouge!** (2001). The attention to period detail and costume design, supervised by Adrian, set new standards for historical accuracy in film. Modern productions like **The Greatest Showman** (2017) and **Chicago** (2002) owe a direct debt to the way **The Great Ziegfeld** balanced spectacle with intimate character moments.
